spine_role: The title-grounding map of the boredom course. Minimal direct boredom content; it justifies why Heidegger keeps the contested title 'metaphysics' for his comprehensive questioning about world/finitude/individuation, by walking the word from physis/logos/aletheia through the post->trans shift of meta and the scholastic decline (Aristotle -> Aquinas -> Suarez), ending (§15) by repurposing 'metaphysics' as the name of the fundamental problem of metaphysics itself and handing into Part One's awakening of a fundamental attunement.

sections.title: The word 'metaphysics'. The meaning of physika: physis as the self-forming prevailing of beings as a whole; logos as taking the prevailing out of concealment; aletheia (truth) as something torn from concealment; the two meanings of physis (a-d)

The two meanings of physis in Aristotle. Questioning concerning beings as a whole and questioning concerning the essentiality (the being) of beings as the dual orientation of questioning in prote philosophia
The formation of the scholastic disciplines of logic, physics, and ethics as the decline of philosophizing proper
The changeover from the technical meaning of meta (after / post) in the word 'metaphysics' to a meaning conceived in terms of content (over beyond / trans)
The inherent incongruities of the traditional concept of metaphysics (trivialized, intrinsically confused, unproblematic)
The concept of metaphysics in Thomas Aquinas as historical evidence for the three features of the traditional concept
The concept of metaphysics in Franz Suarez and the fundamental character of modern metaphysics

Metaphysics as a title for the fundamental problem of metaphysics itself. The result of the preliminary appraisal and the demand to take action in metaphysics on the basis of being gripped by a metaphysical questioning

key_terms.gloss: Customarily 'nature' (Lat. natura/nasci = to be born/arise/grow), but rendered more originarily as 'the self-forming prevailing of beings as a whole' (das von sich selbst her sich bildende Walten des Seienden im Ganzen); broader and more originary than the modern nature/history split; even includes divine beings.
Prevailing as such, the inner essence and inner law of the matter ('the nature of X'); equiprimordial with the regional meaning. In Aristotle this is ousia, the essentiality/being of beings.

Beings that of themselves are always already at hand, forming and passing of their own accord, as opposed to the techne onta (the produced); physis here narrows to a regional concept, a distinctive region of beings.

Speaking-out; the prevailing that has been spoken out. Its fundamental function is to take whatever prevails out of concealment (Entbergen / revealing); opposite of kryptein (concealing). In the logos the prevailing of beings becomes manifest.
Keeping concealed / in concealment; the opposite concept to legein (Verbergen). Established from Heraclitus Frgm. 93 (the Delphic Oracle neither speaks out nor conceals but gives a sign).

Truth, read via the a-privativum as a-letheia, un-concealment (cf. German Un-schuld, Un-endlichkeit): that which is not concealed. Truth is 'something stolen,' torn from concealment in a confrontation in which physis strives to conceal itself; rooted in the fate of human finitude.

Wisdom / lucidity: to say and do the unconcealed as unconcealed, in accordance with the prevailing of things (kata physin), listening out for them (Heraclitus Frgm. 112). The whole physis-logos-aletheia complex is a matter of sophia, i.e., for the philosophers.

Aristotle's name for the most ancient Greek philosophers: not 'physiologists' or 'philosophers of nature' but the genuine primordial title for those who question beings as a whole and bring physis to revealedness.

To stand before a matter and know one's way around in it; only in Aristotle takes on the decided meaning of 'science.' Episteme physike = 'physics' in the broad sense (comprising biology), questioning the whole domain of physis up to the Prime Mover.

The essence/being of beings, that which makes beings beings; still called physis by Aristotle (physis in the second sense). Later 'metaphysica generalis' / ontology considers the on he on under this head.

First Philosophy / prima philosophia / philosophizing proper: Aristotle's unified questioning in a dual orientation — concerning beings as a whole (on katholou / physei onta) AND concerning the being of beings (ousia / protaton genos). How the two orientations form a unity Aristotle left unelaborated; the question is open 'to this day.'

The divine: the ultimate, extreme determinant within the physei onta (the Prime Mover), so named without any particular religious connotation; left to stand as a problem in Aristotle. Grounds the prima-philosophia / theology connection.

Man's stance / self-conduct as a being distinct from nature in the narrower sense (physis); the source of 'ethics.' With physis and logos, one of the three regional themes whose scholastic codification yields the three disciplines.

after / behind / post: the merely positional meaning fixing First Philosophy's place 'behind physics' in the arranged corpus (ta meta ta physika). A title arising from embarrassment, saying nothing about content.

over / beyond / trans: meta in the sense of metabole (changeover, Umschlag), 'turning away from one matter toward another'; First Philosophy as the turn beyond individual beings toward beings in general and the being that properly is — science of the suprasensuous.

Prevailing / holding sway: the core rendering of physis's verbal sense — 'the self-forming prevailing of beings as a whole' — a prevailing man does not have power over but which prevails through and around him.
Revealing / concealing: legein as Entbergen (taking-from-concealment) over against kryptein as Verbergen; the German pair fixes the truth-as-unconcealment reading carried over from Being and Time.

Latin (Aquinas/Descartes/Fichte): the science that governs all other knowledge, most intellectual because it deals with the maxime intelligibilia (the most knowable = most suprasensuous). Aquinas's frame for equating prima philosophia, metaphysica, and theologia.

Latin (Aquinas): 'the most knowable,' divided threefold — ex ordine intelligendi (highest causes / causa prima = God), ex comparatione intellectus ad sensum (the universalia / categories), ex ipsa cognitione intellectus (what is most separate from matter = God and the intelligences). Yields metaphysica = de ente, theologia = de Deo.

Latin (Aquinas): the most general determinations of beings as such (unum, multa, potentia, actus) found 'in via resolutionis,' lying out beyond the physical/sensuous; Aquinas's term anticipating ontology / metaphysica generalis.

Grundstimmung: at the §15->§16 seam the appraisal's negative result issues the demand to 'awaken a fundamental attunement of our philosophizing,' from which the three metaphysical questions must arise in their necessity — the doorway from this map into Part One (the boredom analysis). claims.text: 'Metaphysics' is not a primal word (Urwort) but a relatively late Greek-derived title (ta meta ta physika) that came to designate philosophy; we give the word its meaning from an understanding of philosophy, not the reverse.

physis names the self-forming prevailing of beings as a whole — not modern 'nature,' but a prevailing that runs through man himself, more originary than the nature/history distinction and even including divine beings.

The fundamental function of logos/legein is to take whatever prevails out of concealment (revealing/Entbergen); its opposite is kryptein (concealing). In the logos the prevailing of beings becomes manifest.

physis has in itself a striving to conceal itself (Heraclitus Frgm. 123); hence truth must be wrested from it. aletheia is read as a-letheia, un-concealment: truth is 'something stolen,' torn from concealment, rooted in the finitude of human Dasein — 'nothing to do with proving propositions at the writing desk.'

physis is ambivalent from the start: (alpha) the physei onta as a region opposed to the techne onta, and (beta) prevailing-as-such, the inner essence/law of any matter (= ousia in Aristotle); both meanings persist together and define the questioning of philosophy.

Aristotle amalgamates the two orientations — questioning beings as a whole AND questioning the being (ousia) of beings — as prote philosophia, philosophizing proper; yet how the dual orientation forms a unity he never says, and the question remains open and is no longer even posed today.

The formation of schools (Plato/Xenocrates, Peripatetics, Stoics; evidence in Sextus Empiricus) splits living questioning into logic, physics, ethics; this scholastic ordering is the descent and proper decline of philosophizing proper, which 'begins with' Aristotle.

First Philosophy fit none of the three disciplines, creating an 'embarrassment'; it was filed positionally behind physics — ta meta ta physika — a purely technical title indicating order in the corpus, not content.

When ta meta ta physika was compressed into the Latin 'metaphysica,' meta shifted from positional 'after' (post) to content-bearing 'over/beyond' (trans): metaphysics becomes science/knowledge of the suprasensuous. This changeover is not trivial — 'something essential is decided by it — the fate of philosophy proper in the West.'

The traditional concept of metaphysics is (1) trivialized (the metaphysical = a higher being merely at hand, God/immortal soul), (2) intrinsically confused (it conflates suprasensuous beings with the unsensuous determinations of the being of beings), and (3) unproblematic (it never lets 'metaphysics' itself become a problem).

Aquinas (Prooemium to his commentary on Aristotle's Metaphysics) equates prima philosophia, metaphysica, and theologia/scientia divina via the maxime intelligibile in a threefold sense, brilliantly but in a way essentially determined by faith — holding three disparate directions of questioning together without taking up their intrinsic problematic; for Aquinas metaphysics is in this sense identical with ontology.

The dual orientation harbors a real disharmony — questioning the formal categories (equality, difference, opposition) is something wholly other than the question of the ultimate ground of beings (God); unproblematic in Aristotle, this is raised to a principle in the Middle Ages, where the whole of metaphysics is assigned to knowledge of God.

Franz Suarez (Disputationes metaphysicae, 1597) first undertakes an independent, systematic development of the metaphysical problem (natural theology), decisively shaping modern metaphysics and Descartes; he calls metaphysics 'metaphysica' because it is theology (deals with God), deviating from Aquinas's de ente in communi, and stresses meta=post as the sequence from sensuous to suprasensuous knowledge.

Modern metaphysics (Descartes -> Fichte) is determined by the demand for absolute certainty modeled on mathematical natural science; it places the I/consciousness at the basis as the most secure, unquestioned foundation — a 'comprehensive questioning' that includes the questioner only in a negative sense (the I is precisely NOT put in question).

We take over 'metaphysics' not in its traditional meaning but as the title for the fundamental problem of metaphysics itself — the question 'What is metaphysics, what is philosophizing?' — which inseparably belongs to philosophy and cannot be posed by the sciences about themselves.

The result of the preliminary appraisal is 'thoroughly negative': we have dealt with philosophy but not from out of it. We must now act within metaphysics by letting the three questions (world / finitude / individuation) arise in their necessity from out of a fundamental attunement — 'awakening a fundamental attunement of our philosophizing' is the first proper task of the course.

interlocutors.name: Heraclitus
interlocutors.role: Pre-Socratic authority cited for the physis/logos/aletheia complex: Frgm. 93 (Oracle gives a sign), 123 (physis loves to hide), 112 (sophia = saying/doing the unconcealed kata physin), 54 (hidden harmony stronger than the open), 30 (kosmos as ever-living fire).

interlocutors.name: Aristotle
interlocutors.role: Central source: names the early thinkers physiologoi; develops the dual orientation of prote philosophia (beings as a whole + ousia); designates the ultimate the theion; Sixth Book of the Metaphysics divides First Philosophy into two orientations and names it theologike. The unproblematic dual orientation is the seed Aquinas/Suarez inherit.

interlocutors.name: Plato
interlocutors.role: School-formation begins in his Academy; per Sextus Empiricus the logic/physics/ethics division was prefigured by Plato and first founded by his pupil and Academy-director Xenocrates.

interlocutors.name: Xenocrates
interlocutors.role: Director of the Academy credited (via Sextus Empiricus) with first founding the threefold division of philosophy into logic, physics, ethics — the scholastic codification that decline depends on.

interlocutors.name: Sextus Empiricus
interlocutors.role: Documentary source (Adversus Mathematicos VII.16, ed. Bekker 1842) for the historical claim that the logic/physics/ethics division was prefigured in Plato and introduced by Xenocrates, the Peripatetics, and the Stoics.

interlocutors.name: Thomas Aquinas
interlocutors.role: §13 keystone: equates prima philosophia = metaphysica = theologia/scientia divina via the threefold maxime intelligibile (Prooemium to his Aristotle commentary); metaphysica = de ente (ontology), theologia = de Deo; binds metaphysics to God by faith, raising the Aristotelian disharmony to a principle.

interlocutors.name: Franz Suarez
interlocutors.role: §14: the Spanish Jesuit (1548-1617; Disputationes metaphysicae, 1597) who first develops the metaphysical problem independently and systematically, decisively shaping modern metaphysics and Descartes; calls metaphysics 'metaphysica' because it is theology; placed by Heidegger 'even above Aquinas' in acumen.

interlocutors.name: Descartes
interlocutors.role: Inherits the Suarezian metaphysics (studied at La Fleche; consulted Suarez repeatedly); Meditationes de prima philosophia makes the proof of God's existence and the soul's immortality the objective of First Philosophy; inaugurates the modern demand for absolute certainty.

interlocutors.name: Kant
interlocutors.role: First (after the Christian/modern takeover) to 'get a grip' and make metaphysics itself a problem; cf. Heidegger's own Kant and the Problem of Metaphysics; in Kant 'metaphysics proper' is conceived as theology.

interlocutors.name: Fichte
interlocutors.role: Modern exemplar: Science of Knowledge (Wissenschaftslehre) names the science that has absolute knowledge as its object and thereby grounds metaphysics; epitomizes the certainty-priority of modern metaphysics and the centrality of the I.

bridge_relevance: Title-grounding map, not a boredom analysis. It supplies the conceptual frame within which the King-Salvo bridge's Heideggerian apparatus is licensed: (a) the aletheia-as-unconcealment reading (truth as torn from a self-concealing physis) underwrites the bridge's surface/depth thesis that a phenomenon's truth is wrested from a concealment, not read off the surface; (b) §15's redefinition of 'metaphysics' as the question of what metaphysics itself is, and §16's demand to 'awaken a fundamental attunement,' is the doorway from this map straight into the boredom spine (fcm-03+) on which the bridge actually turns.
